• Apple product runoff: FY2027 handset revenue is modeled at -10% / -16% / -25% in Bull / Base / Bear; management said new-launch modem share is materially below its prior 20% estimate and December-quarter Apple revenue falls about 50% sequentially.
• Memory and manufacturing costs: QCT pricing actions lag contracts and product cycles; Base QCT segment margins start below mature levels and capex remains elevated.
• Execution burden: Base assumes only $3.0B of FY2027 Data Center revenue versus management's $5.0B target; Bear assumes $1.5B.

• Regulatory and licensing: Base QTL revenue falls 3% in FY2027, terminal QTL margin compresses to 64%, and a $250M FY2027 cash charge is included. Bear uses a 10% FY2027 QTL decline, further FY2028–29 contraction, 55% terminal margin and a $1.5B charge.
• China / trade policy: the Bear case slows Handsets, Automotive, Industrial IoT and Data Center rather than applying a vague corporate haircut.
• XR / AR: modeled as a small, loss-making FY2027 option; no assumption that product announcements automatically become material revenue.
• The FY2026 IoT subsegment split is analyst-estimated because Qualcomm reports IoT in aggregate. Do not treat Physical AI or XR revenue as company-disclosed.
